We need to analyze two statements.

First, identify if each has a determinable stance (YES/NO/UNCERTAIN). Need target proposition (specific claim) and stance (FAVOR/AGAINST/UNCERTAIN). Then compare if same proposition.

Manifestation A: Speaker is a parliamentarian (former mayor). She says: "I was harsh... I have hope in this Government regarding social area... He cares for the being... In all ministries aimed at the being we will have better vision of more care for the person." Then: "Instead of demanding execution by Ministry of Justice regarding patrols, Casa da Mulher Brasileira, why not pass that resource directly to the management of Ministry of Women? That's what I question. I don't question that we are in all meanders... Now, I don't agree with that part I cited. How much will be left?" So she is questioning the allocation of resources to Ministry of Justice vs Ministry of Women. She seems to favor moving resources to Ministry of Women. She says "I don't agree with that part I cited." The part cited is presumably the current allocation to Ministry of Justice. So she is against current allocation, favoring direct transfer to Ministry of Women. So there is a stance: She favors transferring resources to Ministry of Women (or opposes current allocation). Is that a specific proposition? Could be "Resources for women's protection (patrols, Casa da Mulher Brasileira) should be managed directly by the Ministry of Women rather than the Ministry of Justice." That's a specific proposition. She expresses support for that (FAVOR). She also says "I don't agree with that part I cited." So stance determinable = YES. Target proposition: "Resources for women's protection programs should be transferred from the Ministry of Justice to the Ministry of Women." Stance: FAVOR (she favors that). Good.

Manifestation B: This is opening of a public hearing on menopause. She declares the hearing open, mentions a tragedy, then describes her role as rapporteur of a bill (PL 5602/2019) creating a program for women in menopause. She says she presented favorable opinion (parecer favorável) to the bill and its apensados, in the form of a substitute that creates the Program. However, she hasn't put the bill to vote yet, awaiting civil society debate. She expresses belief that the hearing will contribute to improving policies. She is not taking a stance on a proposition in this speech; she is describing procedural steps. She endorses the bill (she gave favorable opinion). That could be considered a stance: She favors the bill (the creation of the program). The proposition: "The bill PL 5602/2019 (creating a Program for Attention to Women in Menopause and Climacteric) should be approved." She says she presented favorable opinion. That's a stance FAVOR. But is that a "target proposition" in the speech? She says "Apresentei parecer favorável ao projeto e seus apensados, na forma do substitutivo, que cria o Programa..." So she explicitly states she gave favorable opinion. That's a stance. So stance determinable = YES. Target proposition: "The legislative proposal creating a Program for Attention to Women in Menopause and Climacteric should be approved." Stance: FAVOR.

Now compare if same proposition. Manifestation A about resource allocation between ministries for women's protection. Manifestation B about a bill for menopause program. Different topics. So same_proposition = NO.
